solution_overview:
A car is selected at random from a dealership lot. We are given the probabilities of having a Sunroof ($S$), Leather seats ($L$), and Navigation ($N$), as well as their pairwise intersections and the intersection of all three. We denote these probabilities as follows:

Individual feature probabilities:
$$P(S) = 0.42$$
$$P(L) = 0.55$$
$$P(N) = 0.48$$

Probabilities of having exactly two specified features:
$$P(S \cap L) = 0.25$$
$$P(S \cap N) = 0.22$$
$$P(L \cap N) = 0.30$$

Probability of having all three features:
$$P(S \cap L \cap N) = 0.15$$

Many of the statements relate to the total probability of having at least one feature, which is the union $P(S \cup L \cup N)$. We calculate this using the Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion:

$$P(S \cup L \cup N) = P(S) + P(L) + P(N) - (P(S \cap L) + P(S \cap N) + P(L \cap N)) + P(S \cap L \cap N)$$

$$P(S \cup L \cup N) = 0.42 + 0.55 + 0.48 - (0.25 + 0.22 + 0.30) + 0.15$$

$$P(S \cup L \cup N) = 1.45 - 0.77 + 0.15$$

$$P(S \cup L \cup N) = 0.83$$

We will also need the probabilities of having exactly one feature and exactly two features. Let $P(	ext{exactly one})$ be the probability of having exactly one of the three features, and $P(	ext{exactly two})$ be the probability of having exactly two of the three features.

$P(	ext{exactly two})$ is the sum of pairwise intersections minus three times the triple intersection:

$$P(\text{exactly two}) = (P(S \cap L) + P(S \cap N) + P(L \cap N)) - 3P(S \cap L \cap N)$$

$$P(\text{exactly two}) = (0.25 + 0.22 + 0.30) - 3(0.15)$$

$$P(\text{exactly two}) = 0.77 - 0.45$$

$$P(\text{exactly two}) = 0.32$$

$P(	ext{exactly one})$ is the sum of individual probabilities minus twice the sum of pairwise intersections plus three times the triple intersection:

$$P(\text{exactly one}) = P(S) + P(L) + P(N) - 2(P(S \cap L) + P(S \cap N) + P(L \cap N)) + 3P(S \cap L \cap N)$$

$$P(\text{exactly one}) = 0.42 + 0.55 + 0.48 - 2(0.25 + 0.22 + 0.30) + 3(0.15)$$

$$P(\text{exactly one}) = 1.45 - 2(0.77) + 0.45$$

$$P(\text{exactly one}) = 1.45 - 1.54 + 0.45$$

$$P(\text{exactly one}) = 0.36$$

These derived probabilities will be used in the individual statements.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Having at least one of the three features means the car has $S \cup L \cup N$. From the overview, the probability of this event is:

$$P(S \cup L \cup N) = 0.83$$

The claim states this probability exceeds $80\%$. Since $0.83 = 83\%$, which is greater than $80\%$, the statement is True.

**B.** → True

The probability that the car has exactly one feature is $P(\text{exactly one})$. From the overview, this probability is:

$$P(\text{exactly one}) = 0.36$$

The claim states this probability is above $33\%$. Since $0.36 = 36\%$, which is greater than $33\%$, the statement is True.

**C.** → True

The probability that the car has exactly two features is $P(\text{exactly two})$. From the overview, this probability is:

$$P(\text{exactly two}) = 0.32$$

The claim states this probability is at least $30\%$. Since $0.32 = 32\%$, which is greater than or equal to $30\%$, the statement is True.

**D.** → True

The probability that the car has none of the three features is the complement of having at least one feature. This is $P((S \cup L \cup N)^c) = 1 - P(S \cup L \cup N)$. Using the probability for at least one feature calculated in the overview:

$$P(\text{none}) = 1 - 0.83$$

$$P(\text{none}) = 0.17$$

The claim states this probability is under $20\%$. Since $0.17 = 17\%$, which is less than $20\%$, the statement is True.

**E.** → True

Having at least two features means the car has either exactly two features or exactly three features. These are mutually exclusive outcomes. The probability of having exactly three features is $P(S \cap L \cap N) = 0.15$. The probability of having exactly two features was calculated in the overview:

$$P(\text{at least two}) = P(\text{exactly two}) + P(S \cap L \cap N)$$

$$P(\text{at least two}) = 0.32 + 0.15$$

$$P(\text{at least two}) = 0.47$$

The claim states this probability exceeds $45\%$. Since $0.47 = 47\%$, which is greater than $45\%$, the statement is True.
